conflicts.description: McNeill's 2018 bonus: the original S-1 (2019-03-01) shows only a footnote marker in the Bonus cell (amount 'not yet been determined') and a total of $32,420,826. Both S-1/As, the 424B4 and the 2020 proxy report a $420,000 bonus (approved March 2019) and a total of $32,840,826. The S-1 row is kept as filed with bonus 0.

Elaine Paul's CFO start: the 2021-12-02 8-K announced her appointment 'effective January 3, 2022', but the 2022 proxy says she was appointed 'effective January 4, 2022' and Green was PFO until January 4. The 2023 proxy says she commenced service on 2022-01-04, and her Form 3 event date is 2022-01-04. Recorded as 2022-01-04.

PvP TSR in the 2023 proxy. Footnote (4) says TSR is cumulative from the last trading day before fiscal 2020, but the printed 2021 and 2022 values ($86.97 / $25.79 for Lyft, $133.35 / $71.09 for the peer index) match single-year returns. Using the table's own year-end prices: 42.73/49.13 = 86.97 and 11.02/42.73 = 25.79. The 2024 and 2025 proxies restate the same years on the 2019-12-31 base: Lyft $99.33 / $25.62 (42.73/43.02 and 11.02/43.02), peer $189.64 / $134.82. The 2026 proxy uses a 2020-12-31 base, so its $86.97 for 2021 is correct there. All values are recorded as filed.

PEO coverage wording differs between proxies. The 2024 and 2025 PvP footnotes say Green was PEO for 'fiscal 2020-2023'; the 2026 footnote says 'fiscal 2021-2023' only because its table starts at 2021. These are consistent, not contradictory.

Makavy's end as EVP and Chief Product Officer: the 2020-02-28 8-K announced he 'will no longer serve' in the role (no effective date); the 2020 proxy says he served 'until March 2020'. Recorded at month precision (2020-03).

Llewellyn's start as Chief Legal Officer: the 2025 and 2026 proxies say 'since July 2024' (letter agreement 2024-07-22, effective 'in July 2024'), but her Form 3 gives 2024-08-21 as the date she became a Section 16 officer. The letter itself says that designation would be considered at the August 2024 board meeting. The executive-officer tenure starts 2024-08-21; the title is a few weeks older.

Raj's executive-officer start: proxies date the Head of Rideshare title from August 2021 (interim from March 2021), but his Form 3 gives 2021-10-26. No 8-K reports his designation. Recorded as 2021-10-26 with medium confidence.

open_questions: Raj's exact executive-officer designation date: Form 3 says 2021-10-26 while the Head of Rideshare title dates from August 2021. A board resolution or an 8-K would settle it; none was found.

Lipkovitz's and Makavy's March 2020 effective day is not stated. The 8-K is dated 2020-02-28 and the proxy says March 2020; Lipkovitz's Form 3 event date (2020-03-31) hints the reorganization took effect at month-end. Lipkovitz's March 2021 exit day is also unstated (8-K 2021-03-22 announcement only).

Pre-IPO officer start dates (Green 2007, Zimmer COO 2008-07, President 2013-03, Roberts 2014-11, Sverchek 2012-11 and 2015-10, McNeill 2018-03, Makavy 2017-12 and 2019-02) come only from prospectus and proxy biographies, at month or year precision. Whether Makavy's December 2017 EVP role was an executive-officer role from its start is not stated.

Blackwood-Kapral (Chief Accounting Officer, 2019-2025) was a Section 16 officer but never appeared in a proxy 'executive officers' table. Her CAO row is recorded as an officer title; downstream users may want to exclude it from 'executive officer' tenure.

The FY2026 SCT (2027 proxy, expected around April 2027) will be the first to cover Brewer's retirement (2026-09-28) and any compensation for her successor Michael Brous. Brous is not an NEO in any filed SCT and is not included here.

coverage.method: Summary Compensation Tables extracted from every registration statement and proxy that carries one: S-1 (2019-03-01), both S-1/As (2019-03-18, 2019-03-27), 424B4 (2019-03-29), DEF 14A 2020-2024 and 2026, and the 2025 DEFC14A (the 2025 annual proxy was a contested-solicitation DEFC14A). One comp row per (filing, NEO, fiscal year). FY2017 covers only the two NEOs whose 2017 rows appear (Green, Makavy; Zimmer's 2017 row appears in the 2020 proxy). No Lyft SCT has Option Awards or Pension/NQDC columns. Checked with no SCT: the 2022 10-K/A (a financial restatement, not Part III), the 2025 DEFR14A (board-change supplement), every DEFA14A, and the Engine Capital DEFC14A/PREC14A/DFAN14A. The preliminary PREC14A (2025-04-11) and PRE 14A (2026-03-31) SCT and PvP tables match the definitive filings line for line and are not recorded separately.
Every PvP table (2023, 2024 and 2026 DEF 14A; 2025 DEFC14A). One row per (filing, fiscal year), with each PEO's SCT total and CAP captured separately.

For every NEO: IPO prospectus roster and bios, every proxy 'Executive Officers' section, every 8-K with Item 5.02 in the EDGAR submissions feed through 2026-10-02, each NEO's Form 3, the 2024 CLO letter (10-Q exhibit 10.3), and the separation and transition disclosures in proxies. Day precision comes from 8-K effective dates, proxy CD&A effective dates or Form 3 event dates; pre-IPO and title-change dates are month or year precision from bios. Non-officer roles (advisor or consultant periods, Makavy's EVP Strategic Initiatives, Lipkovitz's EVP Revenue and Market Operations, Llewellyn's pre-2024 General Counsel role) are in notes only.
Pre-IPO officer history comes from prospectus biographies only; earlier non-NEO officers and pre-officer roles are not covered.
